year.label: MRX customer prototype; AMS2 Duratec P4 configuration

identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian customer sports prototype built by Metalmoro as the successor to the MCR, later revised with a new chassis. 'Duratec' denotes the Ford engine and 'P4' the Endurance Brasil class, neither of which is the marque. The constructor states the MRX accepts diverse engine and transmission options, so no single real-world gearbox is fixed and entrants have run different sequential units. The AMS2 car is one such configuration, and its six-speed sequential stick is established by the live drive rather than by a fixed factory specification.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts because a full-throttle clutchless upshift was accepted with an automatic cut detected.
No automatic blip was detected, so the AMS2 car leaves the rev matching to the driver. Whether the real gearbox needs that blip to engage stays unknown, because its construction is not established.
The constructor fixes no transmission for the MRX, so the sequential six-speed is recorded as the configuration modeled in AMS2 rather than a factory specification.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.metalmoro-mrx-duratec-p4.20260813t050853501z-63285bd6 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. The constructor establishes the MRX identity but fixes no transmission, so the real-world gearbox for this exact configuration is not independently confirmed.

claims.basis: The constructor's own page establishes the MRX as a Metalmoro customer prototype, and the exact simulator identity was observed live. The specific real-world build behind the AMS2 Duratec P4 is not identified.

The live drive exercised six sequential gears through a visible sequential stick. The constructor states transmission options vary by customer, so the sequential six-speed is recorded at medium confidence as the configuration modeled in AMS2, not as a fixed factory specification.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

The guided drive accepted a full-throttle clutchless upshift with a detected automatic cut, so no lift is required. No automatic blip was detected on downshifts, and this record follows the curated convention for a sequential stick without automatic blip, where the driver supplies the rev-matching blip.

archetype.basis: Two archetypes survive the gap: stick-6-seq-clutch-start-flat-up-blip-down and stick-6-seq-clutch-start-flat-up-no-blip. They differ only on downshift.manual_blip. A guided drive settles it, by downshifting with no throttle input and seeing whether the gear engages. Also open, though not affecting the choice because both candidates agree there: upshift/throttle_lift.

driver_summary: Six-speed sequential with a lever. The car cuts the upshift, so stay flat. Nothing blips the downshift, and whether this gearbox needs one to engage is not established, so blip anyway: it settles the car into the corner whether or not the box demands it.
